headline: Your brain contains 86 billion neurons—more connections than stars in the Milky Way
universal_truth: The most complex object we know of is the one doing the knowing
fun_facts: Your brain uses 20% of your body's energy despite being only 2% of your weight
You have about 86 billion neurons, each connected to thousands of others
Your brain generates enough electricity to power a small LED light bulb
discussion_questions: What does it mean that the thing studying the brain IS a brain?
How does your brain's complexity compare to computers?
What do you think consciousness actually is?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Three pounds of tissue. 86 billion neurons. 100 trillion connections. The most complex object in the known universe is sitting inside your skull right now, listening to me describe it, aware of itself. The brain studying the brain.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Your brain controls movement, processes senses, stores memories, generates thoughts, and somehow produces consciousness. How does a physical organ create the experience of being you?
cliff.prompt: How does the brain create mind and consciousness?

options.text: We don't fully know—consciousness remains one of science's greatest mysteries
options.response: Honest answer. We know neurons fire and patterns emerge, but how that becomes experience remains mysterious.

options.text: Neurons create consciousness through their electrical and chemical signals
options.response: Neural activity correlates with consciousness, but the HOW remains unsolved...

q1.title: Astronomical Complexity
q1.script: 86 billion neurons, each connected to an average of 7,000 others. That's about 600 trillion synaptic connections—more than the number of stars in the Milky Way. The complexity inside your head exceeds the complexity of the galaxy.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Astronomical Complexity"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Energy Hungry
q2.script: Your brain is 2% of your body weight but uses 20% of your energy. Thinking is metabolically expensive. The brain never truly rests—even during sleep, it's processing, consolidating, maintaining. Consciousness has a constant fuel cost.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Electric Mind
q3.script: Your brain generates about 12-25 watts of electricity—enough to power a small LED bulb. This electricity carries your thoughts, memories, and very sense of self. You are, in a very real sense, electrical.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The most complex object we know of is the one doing the knowing. Your brain is so complex that it can't fully understand itself. That should inspire both wonder and humility.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 87. Tomorrow, we'll discover how lungs breathe for you. Until then, marvel that the thing reading these words is itself a mystery.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Brain Wonder - Appreciate Your Complexity
growTrack.learning_objective: Develop awe for the complexity that enables experience
growTrack.activity: Right now, your brain is interpreting symbols, understanding language, and being aware that it's doing so. Spend a moment in genuine wonder at this. The universe became complex enough to observe itself—through you.
